scope: Bounded keyword and primary-source follow-up. Neither exhaustive priority search nor dynamical-equivalence proof.

filament follower force chaotic dynamics De Canio Lauga Goldstein

sources.title: A three-dimensional morphoelastic model for self-oscillations in polyelectrolyte hydrogel filaments
sources.finding: The source already reports periodic planar and spatial beating, hook rotation, secondary instability and initial-condition dependence. Its physical model is not ours to claim as new.

sources.title: Nonreciprocal oscillations of polyelectrolyte gel filaments subject to a steady and uniform electric field
sources.finding: The authors' abstract reports experiments and a morphoelastic model with flutter/divergence and self-sustained periodic oscillations. This search does not audit every equation or parameter regime of that predecessor.

sources.title: Bifurcations and nonlinear dynamics of the follower force model for active filaments
sources.finding: Clarke, Hwang and Keaveny (2024) describe quasiperiodic states, intermittency and chaotic beating in a three-dimensional tip-driven filament. Broad novelty claims for chaotic active filaments are untenable.

sources.title: Emergent programmable behavior and chaos in dynamically driven active filaments
sources.finding: Krishnamurthy and Prakash (2023) study time-dependent follower forcing and report a transition to chaos. This differs from the steady electric field and evolving internal curvature used here.

interpretation: No matching chaos result for the exact 2026 morphoelastic law was located in this bounded query set. Different forcing laws do not establish inequivalence of attracting dynamics. Historical novelty remains unresolved.
